newsitem.title: USA: Trump loses New Jersey project challenge.
newsitem.headline: Trump loses New Jersey project challenge.

text.p: - A state judge Wednesday rejected Trump Hotels and Casino Resorts' challenge to the financing of a highway project that would serve a potential rival, New Jersey Gov. Christine Whitman said.
"We won the ... case," Whitman said at a press conference as she was handed news of the decision.

Trump, which operates three Atlantic City casinos, had challenged the plan to use revenues of the state Casino Reinvestment Development Authority to help pay for a viaduct easing access to a marina area of Atlantic City where Mirage Resorts Inc is planning a multi-casino development with other operators.

Trump's lawyers had argued that the money should be used for housing the poor, senior citizens or the disabled, under a 1976 amendment to the state constitution that legalized casino gaming in Atlantic City.
The CRDA sought a ruling so it could proceed with a bond issue. It has agreed to pay a $65-million share of the project's $330-million cost.

Lawyers for the state had argued that under a 1993 legal change CRDA was given a new 1.25 percent tax to finance a wider range of investments -- including spurring more hotel construction and a new convention center.
Superior Court Judge Richard Williams ruled that the 1993 law did not violate the state Constitution.
Mirage chief executive Stephen Wynn has called the connector to the Atlantic City Expressway a precondition for his project. Mirage and the state agreed Sept. 18 on a public-private partnership.

Mirage plans a $750-million, 2,000-room hotel-casino to be called Beau Rivage, surrounded by retail and entertainment facilities. Wynn has also brought in two co-developers -- Circus Circus Enterprises Inc and Boyd Gaming Corp. Each has announced plans for a casino-hotel of similar scale, although neither has applied for regulatory approval.
